researched_by: the council's own on-street pay-and-display pages and country park parking pages, its statutory traffic order notices, the 16 May 2025 Executive Member decision record on ModernGov, and local press and parish council reporting of the scheme going live
policy_summary:
SCOPE NOTE: Hampshire County Council is the highway authority for the eleven districts of Hampshire - Basingstoke and Deane, East Hampshire, Eastleigh, Fareham, Gosport, Hart, Havant, New Forest, Rushmoor, Test Valley and Winchester. It is not the highway authority for Portsmouth, Southampton or the Isle of Wight, which are unitary. Since 1 April 2023 it has also run civil parking enforcement on-street across the whole county, having taken that back from the districts; 'responsibility for off-street car parking will remain with district/borough councils'. So almost every car park a van user will meet in Hampshire belongs to a district and is researched separately - except the country parks, which are the county's own land and are in this file.

Hampshire has no provision. No aire, no designated motorhome bays, no waste point, nothing on any council page offering a motorhome anywhere to stay. Its September 2024 residents' survey feeding a new county Parking Strategy asked about safety, availability, payment and enforcement and did not mention motorhomes, campervans or overnight parking at all.

What it has instead is a vehicle-class prohibition attached to on-street pay-and-display schemes, deployed one seafront at a time. Two are live. KEYHAVEN is the important one and it is now made and operating: The Hampshire (New Lane and Saltgrass Lane, Keyhaven) (On-Street Pay-and-Display Parking Places and Prohibition of Waiting) Order 2024 was first advertised on 22 February 2024, re-advertised after amendment on 22 November 2024, approved for making and implementation by Cllr Lulu Bowerman, Executive Member for Highways and Passenger Transport, on 16 May 2025, and went live on 8 December 2025. Charging is GBP1 an hour to GBP8 all day, 10:00-18:00 seven days including bank holidays, payable by card at two machines in New Lane or through RingGo code 85161; blue badge holders are free. Overlaid on every bay is 'No Motor Caravans 8pm - 8am'. The council's own page renders it as 'No motorhomes 8pm to 8am'. That is an outright ban, not a charge: between 20:00 and 08:00 a motor caravan may not be on those bays at any price.

BARTON ON SEA did not follow. The parallel Hampshire (Barton-on-Sea, New Forest) (On-Street Pay-and-Display Parking Places) Order 2024, advertised the same day and carrying the same 'No Motor Caravans 8pm - 8am' line across roughly 640 metres of pay-and-display bays plus the limited-waiting and free bays on Marine Drive East, Marine Drive West and Barton Court Avenue, was DEFERRED at the same 16 May 2025 decision day. The director of universal services asked for more time 'to look at the business case' and said 'we'll be bringing this back in due course'. It had not returned as at July 2026. Barton therefore still has only the 'No overnight parking' signs Hampshire put up on the clifftop as an interim measure, which the council itself said 'will not have a Traffic Regulation Order so are not enforceable, but will hopefully deter some of this parking'. A residents' petition had reported at least twenty vans overnight on Marine Drive East in a single weekend. Barton is the clearest example in the dataset of a seafront where the restriction is entirely signage and entirely bluff.

The third live case is LEE-ON-THE-SOLENT, which nobody writes about. Hampshire's own on-street page for Marine Parade West carries the flat line 'No overnight stay for motor caravans' alongside a 10:00-18:00 GBP1.50-to-GBP9.00 tariff. It predates the New Forest schemes and was cited by the council in 2023 as the model for what it intended to do at Barton. None of Hampshire's other on-street pay-and-display towns - Basingstoke, Eastleigh, Fareham, Hart, Lymington, Rushmoor, Winchester - carries any motorhome or overnight wording.

On the county's own land the rule is simpler and older. Hampshire runs five country parks - Lepe, Queen Elizabeth, River Hamble, Royal Victoria and Staunton - all now on ANPR with seasonal tariffs and annual passes. Queen Elizabeth Country Park, which straddles the A3 at Butser Hill inside the South Downs National Park, says it plainly on its parking page: the forest and Butser car parks 'are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week', and 'overnight parking is not permitted'. That combination - gates that never close and a rule that says do not stay - is the single most useful thing to know about Butser Hill, because the open barrier reads as an invitation and is not one. Lepe does the opposite and simply closes: 07:00-22:00 April to September, 07:00-19:00 October to March, with the Western car park shut altogether from November to March.

NO LAY-BY ORDER WAS FOUND. Searches for motor caravan or overnight prohibitions on Hampshire's trunk and A-road lay-bys returned nothing, and there is no county-wide instrument of any kind against sleeping in a vehicle. Outside the three named seafronts and the country park car parks, Hampshire has made no rule a van user can break.

sites.name: New Lane and Saltgrass Lane, Keyhaven
sites.search_hint: Saltgrass Lane and New Lane, Keyhaven, Milford on Sea
sites.notes:
MADE AND LIVE. The Hampshire (New Lane and Saltgrass Lane, Keyhaven) (On-Street Pay-and-Display Parking Places and Prohibition of Waiting) Order 2024. Advertised 22 February 2024, re-advertised after amendment 22 November 2024 (objection deadline 13 December 2024, ref A2039/MJB), approved for making and implementation by Cllr Lulu Bowerman on 16 May 2025 after 63 consultation responses of which 34 objected, and in operation since 8 DECEMBER 2025.

The scheme has two limbs. By day, pay and display 10:00-18:00 Monday to Sunday including bank holidays, GBP1 for one hour rising to GBP8 all day, two card machines in New Lane or RingGo code 85161, blue badge holders free, plus two lengths of free one-hour limited waiting on Saltgrass Lane North (no return within two hours) and five new lengths of double yellow line. By night, 'No Motor Caravans 8pm - 8am' across every pay-and-display and limited-waiting bay on both roads. Hampshire's own page states it as 'No motorhomes 8pm to 8am'.

The overnight limb is a prohibition, not a tariff - there is no price at which a motorhome may stay. Everything else parks free from 18:00 to 10:00. This is the sharpest live example in southern England of an authority pricing the day and banning the vehicle class at night.

On applies_to: the sibling Barton notice defines a motor caravan as 'any vehicle constructed or adapted for use as a mobile place of sleeping accommodation or any vehicle being put to such use, whether on a temporary or permanent basis, and regardless of whether or not the vehicle also retains a different use'. That is a use test as much as a body-type test and reaches far wider than a DVLA motor caravan - it catches a self-converted panel van and, read literally, a car with someone sleeping in it. The Keyhaven public notice does not reprint the definition, but the two orders were drafted together and advertised on the same day, so the same wording is very likely. Recorded here as adapted_for_sleeping on that basis; verify against the sealed order before relying on it.

Why it happened: Cllr Fran Carpenter described 'visible litter on the marsh, campervans - some as big as buses - packed as far as the eye could see' and the seafront resembling 'a camp site'; up to 60 vans were reported at peak. Cllr Bowerman noted 'there are no public facilities overnight for parking'. Nothing was provided in exchange.
sites.geocode_precision: the New Lane parking area by the Cut Bridge junction with Saltgrass Lane on Hurst Spit; the restriction runs along both roads

sites.name: Marine Parade West, Lee-on-the-Solent
sites.notes:
The forgotten one. Hampshire's own on-street pay-and-display page for Lee-on-the-Solent carries a single flat line - 'No overnight stay for motor caravans' - under a 10:00-18:00 Monday to Sunday tariff of GBP1.50 for an hour to GBP9.00 all day, card or RingGo only, no cash, blue badge holders free. No hours are published for the motor caravan restriction, unlike Keyhaven's explicit 20:00-08:00, and no order title or making date could be traced, so time_from and time_to are left unset and confidence is medium.

It matters because it is the precedent. When residents petitioned for restrictions on Marine Drive West at Barton on Sea in 2023, Hampshire's published response pointed to Lee-on-the-Solent as the comparable work it had recently done. Lee is the template; Keyhaven is the template applied.

Do not confuse this with Gosport Borough Council's Marine Parade car parks a few yards away, which are off-street and the borough's.
sites.geocode_precision: PO13 9ED postcode centroid on Marine Parade West, the seafront road; the pay-and-display bays run along it

sites.name: Marine Drive East and Marine Drive West, Barton on Sea (advisory signs)
sites.search_hint: Marine Drive East and Marine Drive West, Barton on Sea, New Milton
sites.notes:
SIGNS WITHOUT A SIGN. Hampshire installed 'No overnight parking' signs on the Barton clifftop, at the west end of Marine Drive East, as an explicitly interim measure, and said of them: they 'will not have a Traffic Regulation Order so are not enforceable, but will hopefully deter some of this parking'. The council also accepted that its 'enforcement powers are limited because there are no parking restrictions in place'. Residents reported at least twenty vans overnight along Marine Drive East in a single weekend.

Recorded as a separate in-force record from the deferred order because the legal effect is completely different and a van user needs both halves: there are signs, they say no overnight parking, and as at July 2026 nothing stands behind them. Park4night contributors have been arguing about exactly this since 2021 - 'new signage just gone up ... absolutely no overnight parking attached to all the lamp posts' against 'there is no enforcement in place to stop overnight parking and or sleeping on this road'. Both are correct.

The adjacent Marine Drive car parks are New Forest District Council's, where Article 12 of its 2005 order does ban sleeping and is enforceable - see new-forest-district.json.
sites.geocode_precision: Marine Drive West clifftop opposite number 24; the signs and the proposed bays run along Marine Drive East and West

sites.name: Marine Drive East, Marine Drive West and Barton Court Avenue, Barton on Sea (proposed 2024 order, deferred)
sites.search_hint: Hampshire Barton-on-Sea New Forest On-Street Pay and Display Parking Places Order 2024
sites.notes:
DEFERRED, NOT REFUSED, AND NOT YET BACK. The Hampshire (Barton-on-Sea, New Forest) (On-Street Pay-and-Display Parking Places) Order 2024 was advertised on 22 November 2024 alongside the Keyhaven order and went to the same decision day on 16 May 2025. Cllr Bowerman approved Keyhaven; on Barton, Patrick Blogg, director of universal services, deferred the recommendations 'to allow officers more time to look at the business case' and said 'we'll be bringing this back in due course'. No further decision, notice or report was found up to July 2026.

What it would do if made: pay and display 10:00-18:00 seven days including bank holidays on about 434m of the south side of Marine Drive East and about 206m of the south side of Marine Drive West, GBP1 an hour to GBP8 all day (season tickets GBP194 a month to GBP1,168 a year), free outside those hours; free two-hour limited waiting with no return within two hours on Marine Drive North either side of the Barton Court Avenue junction, on Marine Drive South and the service road, and 15m of Barton Court Avenue West; new no waiting at any time near Sandmartin Close and Christchurch Bay Road; and, across ALL of it - pay and display, limited waiting and free bays alike - 'No Motor Caravans 8pm - 8am'.

The definition clause is the find. The notice defines a motor caravan as 'any vehicle constructed or adapted for use as a mobile place of sleeping accommodation or any vehicle being put to such use, whether on a temporary or permanent basis, and regardless of whether or not the vehicle also retains a different use'. The second limb - 'any vehicle being put to such use' - converts a body-type prohibition into a use-based one and is materially wider than Devon's Schedule 14 test or the DVLA body code that most authorities lean on. If this order is ever made, it is the wording to quote.

Opposition was strong and political rather than public-order: businesses said the charges would harm trade, a New Milton town councillor was refused permission to speak at the decision day, and a county councillor called the scheme a 'threat to democracy'. The overnight motorhome limb was not the contested part. That is why the deferral is about the business case for charging, and why the motorhome ban is being held hostage to a revenue argument it has nothing to do with.

sites.name: Butser Hill car park, Queen Elizabeth Country Park
sites.search_hint: Butser Hill car park, Queen Elizabeth Country Park, Petersfield
sites.notes:
The trap. Hampshire's own parking page says both things on the same screen: 'Forest and Butser car parks are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week' and 'overnight parking is not permitted'. No barrier, no closing time, and a rule you will only find if you read the website. ANPR runs the whole park - 'our automatic number plate recognition system means you'll only pay for the time you've spent at the park' - which means an overnight stay is recorded automatically as a long stay whether or not anyone walks past the van.

Tariffs are seasonal: GBP2 to GBP7 October to March, GBP2.50 to GBP9.50 April to September, motorbikes free, coaches GBP20, blue badge holders pay the standard rate. An annual pass is GBP85 (GBP65 blue badge) and covers five Hampshire country parks - it buys parking, not a night.

Butser Hill is the high open down on the west side of the A3 with toilets, a kiosk and the best views in the eastern South Downs, and it is a magnet for van overnighting for exactly that reason. It sits inside the South Downs National Park but the land, the car park and the rule are Hampshire's, not the Authority's - see south-downs-national-park.json, which correctly attributes it here.

No instrument was found behind the rule. Nothing suggests an off-street parking order or a byelaw; it reads as landowner policy enforced through the ANPR contract, which is why enforcement is anpr and instrument is landowner_policy rather than off_street_parking_order.
sites.geocode_precision: coordinates published by Hampshire County Council on its own Queen Elizabeth Country Park parking page for the Butser Hill car park

sites.name: Queen Elizabeth Country Park forest car parks (visitor centre, Gravel Hill, Benham's, Upper and Lower Windmill, Juniper and Lower Juniper)
sites.search_hint: Queen Elizabeth Country Park visitor centre, Gravel Hill, Horndean
sites.notes:
The seven car parks on the forest side of the A3, opposite Butser Hill. Same regime: open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, ANPR, seasonal tariffs GBP2-GBP7 winter and GBP2.50-GBP9.50 summer, and 'overnight parking is not permitted'.

Worth separating from Butser Hill because the ownership split confuses people. Forestry England manages the woodland, the trails and the mountain bike centre at Queen Elizabeth and sells its own passes; the CAR PARKS, the ANPR and the overnight rule are Hampshire County Council's. A Forestry England pass or Discovery Pass does not answer the parking question here.
sites.geocode_precision: PO8 0QE, the park address at Gravel Hill, Horndean, given by Hampshire County Council; the visitor centre and six further car parks lie around it

sites.name: Lepe Country Park (Clifftop, Beach and Western car parks)
sites.search_hint: Lepe Country Park car park, Exbury, Southampton
sites.notes:
Lepe solves the problem by closing rather than by prohibiting. Three car parks - Clifftop, Beach and Western - open 07:00 to 22:00 from April to September and 07:00 to 19:00 from October to March, with the Western car park shut altogether from November to March. time_from and time_to record the summer closure; in winter the gap runs 19:00 to 07:00.

Tariffs match the other country parks: GBP2-GBP7 October to March, GBP2.50-GBP9.50 April to September, motorbikes free, coaches by advance booking at GBP20, and the GBP85 five-park annual pass applies. Unlike Queen Elizabeth, the parking page carries no explicit 'overnight parking is not permitted' sentence - the hours do the work, and being inside the gates after closing is the contravention.

This is the Solent shore facing the Isle of Wight, three miles of beach and the D-Day embarkation hards, and it is exactly the kind of place a van user would try. It is also inside the New Forest National Park while being Hampshire County Council land - one of the two county car parks the National Park Authority refers to without naming.
sites.geocode_precision: SO45 1AD, the Lepe Country Park postcode in Exbury and Lepe parish; corroborated by the OS grid reference SZ450986 for Lepe

sites.name: Staunton Country Park, Havant
sites.search_hint: Staunton Country Park, Middle Park Way, Havant PO9 5HB
sites.notes:
Hampshire's country park at Middle Park Way, Havant, on ANPR with the cheapest tariff of the five - GBP2-GBP4.50 October to March and GBP2.50-GBP6.50 April to September, farm parking free. Published hours of 10:00-17:00 April to October and 10:00-16:00 November to March are given for the farm and gardens, not explicitly for the car park, and the parking page itself could not be reached (404). No overnight statement is published.

Status recorded as unknown and confidence low deliberately: it is certain that Hampshire owns and ANPR-monitors this car park, and near-certain that overnight parking is unwelcome, but no published rule or closing time for the car park was found. Do not present this to a user as a confirmed restriction without checking on the ground.
sites.geocode_precision: PO9 5HB, the park address given by Hampshire County Council

sites.name: Royal Victoria Country Park, Netley
sites.search_hint: Royal Victoria Country Park, Netley Abbey, Southampton SO31 5RA
sites.notes:
Five car parks on Southampton Water at Netley, ANPR-managed, GBP2-GBP7 October to March and GBP2.50-GBP9.50 April to September, blue badge and EV bays, GBP85 five-park annual pass. The council says the 'park grounds are accessible at all times' while reserving the right to restrict access for safety or operational reasons.

UNLIKE Queen Elizabeth, Royal Victoria publishes no overnight parking rule and no closing time. That is why status is unknown and confidence low rather than in_force: the ANPR will record an overnight stay, but nothing published says it is prohibited. This is a genuine gap in Hampshire's own publication, not an inference that overnighting is allowed.
sites.geocode_precision: coordinates published by Hampshire County Council on its own Royal Victoria Country Park visitor page

notes:
THE HEADLINE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THIS FILE WAS OPENED TO SETTLE: Keyhaven is made and live. The 16 May 2025 decision record shows Cllr Lulu Bowerman approving 'a Traffic Order to be made and implemented under the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984', and the charges and the 20:00-08:00 motor caravan ban came into operation on 8 DECEMBER 2025 with two card machines in New Lane and RingGo code 85161. Park4night contributors confirm it from the other side - 'since December no campers and motorhomes allowed'. Barton on Sea was deferred at the same meeting for work on the business case and had not come back as at July 2026; its clifftop still has only advisory signs that Hampshire has publicly admitted are unenforceable.

The shape of Hampshire's instrument is worth carrying forward. It does not make standalone motorhome prohibition orders the way Devon added lengths of road to Schedule 14. It bolts 'No Motor Caravans 8pm - 8am' onto an on-street PAY-AND-DISPLAY order. That has two consequences. First, the motorhome ban travels with the charging scheme, so it only appears where the county also wants revenue - which is why Keyhaven got it, Barton did not, and Lymington, Fareham, Eastleigh, Basingstoke, Winchester, Hart and Rushmoor have charging without any motorhome wording at all. Second, and this is the one that bit at Barton, the motorhome limb can be blocked by an argument that has nothing to do with motorhomes. Barton's overnight ban was uncontroversial; the charges were not; the whole scheme stalled on the business case. An authority that wants to stop overnight parking and nothing else can do it in a few weeks with a prohibition of waiting order. Hampshire chose the vehicle that carries a revenue case and inherited the revenue case's opponents.

The definition clause in the Barton notice is the most transferable text found this session: a motor caravan is 'any vehicle constructed or adapted for use as a mobile place of sleeping accommodation OR ANY VEHICLE BEING PUT TO SUCH USE, whether on a temporary or permanent basis, and regardless of whether or not the vehicle also retains a different use'. Most vehicle-class bans in this dataset are body-type tests that a car camper or an unconverted panel van walks straight through. This one is not. It is a use test wearing a body-type label, and if the same wording is in the sealed Keyhaven order then Keyhaven catches far more than motorhomes.

DIRECTION OF TRAVEL: tightening, slowly, and with no compensating provision anywhere. Hampshire made one seafront ban in 2025, has a second sitting deferred, already had a third at Lee-on-the-Solent, and offers not one legal overnight space in a county with 45 miles of Solent and Christchurch Bay coast. The county's own words in the Keyhaven papers - 'there are no public facilities overnight for parking, and campers use the local land' - diagnose the problem correctly and then do nothing about it. Its September 2024 parking strategy survey did not ask a single question about motorhomes. Compare South Ayrshire, where the same diagnosis (chemical waste in the harbour) produced bays, a fee and a waste point.

The displacement picture in the New Forest is now genuinely bad and Hampshire owns one part of it. Forestry England began charging across the New Forest on 20 April 2026 at up to GBP8; New Forest District Council's Article 12 bans sleeping in all 51 of its car parks; Hampshire closed Keyhaven in December 2025. Three authorities tightened within twelve months of each other, none of them created anywhere to go, and the only stretch of coast still open at night is the Barton clifftop, which is open only because a business case stalled.

WATCH OUT FOR ATTRIBUTION ERRORS in this area. Butser Hill and the Queen Elizabeth car parks are Hampshire's, not the South Downs National Park Authority's and not Forestry England's, even though Forestry England runs the forest around them. Hayling Island's beachfront car park, where motorhomes were permanently banned from staying overnight, is Havant Borough Council's off-street land, not Hampshire's, and belongs in a Havant file. Gosport's Marine Parade car parks are the borough's; the Marine Parade West on-street bays a few yards away are Hampshire's. Since 1 April 2023 the line is clean and easy to apply: if the vehicle is on the highway it is Hampshire's, if it is in a car park it is the district's - except in a country park, where it is Hampshire's again.
open_questions: Does the sealed Keyhaven order carry the same 'or any vehicle being put to such use' definition of motor caravan that the Barton notice publishes? The Keyhaven public notice does not reprint the interpretation clause and the made order was not found online. This determines whether the Keyhaven ban is a body-type test or a use test, which is the difference between it catching coachbuilts only and it catching every self-converted van and car camper on the spit.

What has happened to the Barton-on-Sea order since the 16 May 2025 deferral? No decision, report or fresh notice was found up to July 2026. Officers were to 'look at the business case' and bring it back 'in due course'. Check Hampshire's Executive Member for Highways decision days and public notices.

Which order made the Lee-on-the-Solent 'No overnight stay for motor caravans' restriction, when, and what hours does it actually run? Hampshire's page gives the rule but no times and no order title, so the record here has no time_from or time_to.

How many PCNs has Hampshire issued at Keyhaven for the 20:00-08:00 motor caravan contravention since 8 December 2025, and does it patrol at night? Enforcement is civil and the machines are unattended; the whole point of the order is a window when nobody is normally working.

Does Royal Victoria Country Park have any published overnight parking rule or car park closing time? Its pages say the grounds are 'accessible at all times' and say nothing about overnighting, which is the only one of the five country parks with no rule found either way.
River Hamble Country Park was not researched - both its visit and parking pages returned 404 this session. It is the fifth Hampshire country park and needs a record.

Is there an off-street parking order or a byelaw behind the country park car parks, or is 'overnight parking is not permitted' purely contractual landowner policy enforced through the ANPR operator? The instrument determines whether a notice is a PCN or a private parking charge, and nothing published says which.
Did the county Parking Strategy that the September 2024 residents' survey fed into ever get published, and does it mention motorhomes? The survey itself did not.
